newsitem.title: UK: Yieh Phui seeks approval for bond buyback.
newsitem.headline: Yieh Phui seeks approval for bond buyback.

text.p: Yieh Phui Enterprise Co Ltd is seeking regulatory approval to buy back, at par, its $90 million convertible bond, it said in a statement on Wednesday.
Yieh Phui said it expected it would take a month to get approval for the buyback and that Bankers Trust, lead manager of the deal, would be the repurchasing agent.

The statement said: "Yieh Phui acknowledges that as a result of the false invoice investigation recently by the Investigation Bureau of the ROC (Republic of China), the company's stock and convertible bond prices have suffered considerable volatility".
"While Yieh Phui denies these unfounded allegations ...(it) does want to give investors the choice of selling the convertible bonds back to the company at par."
There were reports in late June that Yieh Phui had issued fraudulent invoices, a claim it immediately denied.

The convertible notes, with a 10-year maturity and carrying a 1.00 percent coupon, have a conversion price of NT$38.38 per share, which represented a seven percent premium at the time of pricing. The stock closed at NT$25.30 today.
